title: AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer - Associate (SOA-C03)
summary: AWS Certified CloudOps Engineer - Associate (SOA-C03) is an associate-level certification for practitioners who build and operate on AWS. The exam is organised into 5 content domains: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization (22%), Reliability and Business Continuity (22%), Deployment, Provisioning, and Automation (22%), Security and Compliance (16%), Networking and Content Delivery (18%). It is delivered as 50 scored questions and 15 unscored, scored against a scaled pass mark of 720 out of 1,000 with no per-domain minimum, so strength in one domain offsets weakness in another. Every task statement in this topic carries a MEDIUM and a HARD exercise batch, so the practice material follows the published outline of the exam rather than a general reading list. The statements here are taken from the exam guide, and the task list is the one AWS publishes: if AWS revises the guide, this topic is revised with it.
objectives: Monitoring, Logging, Analysis, Remediation, and Performance Optimization: the guide's domain 1 focus, examined through its 3 task statement(s).
Reliability and Business Continuity: the guide's domain 2 focus, examined through its 3 task statement(s).
Deployment, Provisioning, and Automation: the guide's domain 3 focus, examined through its 2 task statement(s).
Security and Compliance: the guide's domain 4 focus, examined through its 2 task statement(s).
Networking and Content Delivery: the guide's domain 5 focus, examined through its 3 task statement(s).

beginner.definition: This is a professional certificate from Amazon Web Services, often shortened to AWS, that proves you can run systems in their cloud. It is an associate level exam, which means it expects some real hands-on time with the platform. The exam code is SOA-C02 and the full name is AWS Certified SysOps Administrator. SysOps simply means system operations, the work of keeping services healthy after they are built.
beginner.whyItMatters: Many companies now rent their computers from a cloud provider instead of owning servers. They need people who can keep those rented systems fast, safe and cheap. This certificate proves you have done that work, not just read about it. It helps you move from a help desk or junior administrator job into a cloud operations role. Employers also use it as evidence that you understand monitoring, backups and access control in a real account.
howItWorks: Start by getting comfortable with the AWS console and the command line interface, because you must actually build and fix things rather than only answer theory questions.
Study each exam domain in turn, and for every topic create the resource yourself in a free test account and then delete it again.
Practise reading logs and metrics so you can explain why a service is slow, failing or more expensive than expected.
Learn the shared responsibility model, meaning which security tasks belong to AWS and which belong to you.
Take practice tests to find weak areas, then go back to the console and rebuild those parts by hand.
On exam day you answer multiple choice questions and also complete lab tasks inside a live AWS environment.
beginner.example: Imagine you rent a flat instead of buying a house. The landlord keeps the building standing, but you still decide who gets a key, what furniture fits and when to call a repair service. Cloud computing works the same way. AWS keeps the data centres running, and you decide who can log in, how much space you use and what happens when a hard disk fails. A SysOps administrator is the person who holds the keys, watches the electricity bill and knows which fuse to reset at two in the morning.
takeaways: You need hands-on time in a real AWS account, because the lab questions test practical actions, not just memory.
Operations work is about monitoring, security, reliability and cost, so study all four together rather than separately.
Always check the current exam guide on the AWS website, because services and domain weights change over time.
